article.title: Why Training on the Most Recent Data Is Not Always Best
article.why: Balance freshness with representativeness when choosing a training window.

paragraphs.en:
Teams often assume that the newest data should dominate model training. Recent observations feel more relevant because they are closer to the future scoring period. That intuition is useful, but it can fail when the latest period is unusual. A short recent window may be fresh yet unrepresentative.

Suppose a retailer trains a purchase model using only the latest six months. During those months, the company ran a large points campaign, changed store hours, and introduced a new payment feature. Customer behavior during this period may differ sharply from normal conditions. A model trained only on these months can learn temporary patterns that disappear after the campaign ends.

This creates a trade-off between freshness and representativeness. Older data may contain outdated relationships, but it can also provide more examples of ordinary seasonality, stable customer behavior, and rare outcomes. Recent data may reflect the newest environment while being dominated by one event. The best training window depends on which source of error is more dangerous.

Seasonality makes the problem even harder. If a model trained in summer is used during winter, category mix, travel, household spending, and promotion response may change. Using twelve or twenty-four months can capture a full seasonal cycle, while a three-month window cannot. On the other hand, if a major product or policy change occurred recently, older seasons may no longer be comparable.

Teams should therefore examine performance by time rather than selecting a window by habit. One approach is rolling backtesting: train on several candidate windows and evaluate each model on later periods. For example, compare models trained on the last six, twelve, twenty-four, and thirty-six months using the same future validation periods. The goal is not to find the window with the best training score, but the one that generalizes most reliably.

Another issue is concept drift. The relationship between features and outcomes can change even if the feature distributions look similar. A customer characteristic that predicted conversion two years ago may become less useful after pricing, channel, or product changes. In that case, giving very old observations the same weight as recent observations can hurt performance.

Recency weighting can provide a middle ground. Instead of removing older data completely, the model can assign greater weight to recent observations while retaining older examples. This is not always necessary, but it can help when relationships change gradually rather than suddenly.

Rare events also influence window design. If the positive class is extremely uncommon, using only recent data may leave too few positive examples for stable learning. A longer window can improve statistical support, provided the historical positives are still comparable to current cases.

Operational definitions must be aligned across time as well. A feature may have the same column name across three years but different business logic because a source system changed. Combining such data without version checks can create artificial patterns. Data lineage and schema history are therefore part of training-window design.

A practical decision process asks: What changed in the business? Which periods are comparable? Does the candidate window include complete seasonal cycles? Are there enough positive examples? Do feature definitions remain stable? Which window performs best on multiple future periods rather than one lucky test set?

The newest data is important, but ‘newest’ is not the same as ‘best.’ Good training data should resemble the environment in which the model will make decisions. Sometimes that means emphasizing recent months. Sometimes it means keeping a longer history to avoid overreacting to a temporary event. Training-window design is therefore a modeling decision, not a simple preference for freshness.
paragraphs.zh:
團隊常假設最新資料應該主導 model training，因為 recent observations 更接近未來 scoring period。但當最新期間本身很特殊時，這個直覺會失效：recent window 可以很 fresh，卻不具代表性。

例如零售商只用最近6個月訓練 purchase model，而這段期間正好有大型 point campaign、營業時間調整與新支付功能。此時 customer behavior 可能偏離平常狀態，model 會學到 campaign 結束後就消失的 temporary pattern。

這形成 freshness 與 representativeness 的 trade-off。Older data 可能含過時關係，但也提供正常 seasonality、穩定行為與 rare outcome 的更多例子。Recent data 比較貼近現況，卻可能被單一事件主導。最佳 training window 取決於哪一種 error risk 更大。

Seasonality 讓問題更複雜。夏季資料拿去預測冬季時，category mix、travel、household spending、promotion response 都可能變。12或24個月可涵蓋完整 seasonal cycle，但若最近發生重大制度或 product change，older seasons 又可能失去可比性。

因此應以時間切分來比較 performance，而不是習慣性選固定 window。可用 rolling backtesting，分別以6、12、24、36個月訓練，再用後續多個期間驗證，找出最穩定 generalize 的 window，而不是只看 training score。

Concept drift 也重要。即使 feature distribution 看起來類似，feature 與 target 的關係也可能改變；定價、channel、product 變更都可能讓舊 pattern 失效。

Recency weighting 是折衷方式：保留較舊資料，但讓較新的 observation 權重更高，適合關係逐步變化而非突然斷裂的情境。

Rare positive 也會影響設計。若正例極少，window 太短會讓正例不足、variance 變大；較長 window 可增加統計支撐，但前提是歷史正例仍可比較。

另外要確認 feature definition 跨期一致。相同 column name 不代表 business logic 相同，source system 變更也可能製造 artificial pattern。

實務上要一起問：business 發生什麼變化？哪些期間可比？是否涵蓋完整 seasonality？正例是否足夠？feature definition 是否穩定？哪個 window 在多個 future periods 表現最穩定？

最新資料很重要，但 newest 不等於 best。Training window 是 modeling decision，不只是偏好 freshness。
paragraphs.ja:
model trainingでは最新dataを重視したくなりますが、最新期間が特殊ならshort recent windowはfreshでもrepresentativeとは限りません。

例えば直近6か月に大型point campaign、営業時間変更、新payment featureが集中していれば、その期間のcustomer behaviorは通常状態と異なる可能性があります。そのdataだけで学習するとcampaign終了後に消えるtemporary patternをmodelが学びます。

ここではfreshnessとrepresentativenessのtrade-offがあります。古いdataはoutdatedな関係を含む一方、通常seasonality、安定行動、rare outcomeを多く含められます。recent dataは現在に近いですが一つのeventに支配されることがあります。

seasonalityも重要です。summer dataだけでwinterを予測するとcategory mixやpromotion responseが変わることがあります。12か月や24か月ならseasonal cycleを含められますが、最近大きな制度変更があれば古いseasonは比較できないかもしれません。

そのためrolling backtestingで複数windowを比較します。6、12、24、36か月などでtrainし、同じfuture validation periodsで評価します。training scoreではなく将来期間で安定してgeneralizeするwindowを選びます。

concept driftにも注意します。feature distributionが似ていても、featureとtargetの関係はpricing、channel、product変更で変わります。古いobservationを同じweightで使うと性能低下につながることがあります。

recency weightingは中間案です。古いdataを捨てず、recent observationへ大きなweightを与えます。

positive caseが極端に少ない場合、短いwindowでは正例不足でvarianceが大きくなるため、比較可能なhistorical positivesを残す価値があります。

feature definitionの時点整合も必要です。同じcolumn名でもsource system変更でlogicが変わっていればartificial patternを学ぶ可能性があります。

business change、seasonality、positive数、definition stability、複数future periodsでのperformanceを一緒に見てtraining windowを決めるべきです。newestは重要ですが、bestとは限りません。
